name: Mumbai Nagar Seva — BMC Civic Complaint Resolution 2018–2024 (Kaggle competition data; SYNTHETICALLY GENERATED)
publisher: Kaggle competition host (not verified from the primary page by this tooling). The dataset is described as synthetically generated. It is NOT official BMC complaint data and NOT a BMC / Government of Maharashtra open-data release or API.
role_summary: Large-scale Mumbai/BMC-STRUCTURED SYNTHETIC civic dataset: synthetic training/stress-testing of structured pipelines, taxonomy coverage, routing/triage pipeline testing, analytics demonstrations and leakage testing. NOT real-world validation; kept separate from genuinely real Indian datasets in every report.
version_note: Per the Kaggle competition information (reported by the repository owner, 2026-10-01): the dataset is SYNTHETICALLY GENERATED rather than a collection of actual BMC complaint records. Per a web-search summary of the Kaggle data page (secondary): ~1.2M complaints, Jan 2018–Dec 2024, all 24 BMC wards; files bmc_train.csv (960,000 rows, 35 features + target `citizen_satisfied`), bmc_test.csv (240,000 rows, 34 features, target WITHHELD) and bmc_data_dictionary.csv. Competition task: predict citizen satisfaction with the resolution. Exact column names are NOT known to us until the file is profiled; the exact generation method is NOT established by anything recorded here.

data_access.method: Kaggle competition data: attach the competition as a notebook input (accept the competition rules on Kaggle first); it is read in place from /kaggle/input and is never downloaded or copied by this repository.
data_access.data_dictionary: bmc_data_dictionary.csv ships with the data: read it, then assign every column to a role explicitly (see mappings/bmc_mumbai_columns.v1.json and `cli profile bmc_mumbai`).

origin_notes: The competition RULES are reported (by the repository owner) to state explicitly that this dataset is synthetically generated, not a collection of actual BMC complaint records. It must never be presented as real-world BMC validation, official BMC data, or evidence of real citizen behaviour.

Because the data is synthetic its free-text columns (if any) are not citizen-written, so they can never be confirmed as citizen narratives, and nothing here supports a real Hindi/Marathi/Hinglish claim.

Per the Competition Rules (2026-10-02): the dataset is synthetically generated and does not represent real citizens or actual complaint records. The generation method is not documented anywhere we hold.
subset_used: Train file only (the test file's target is withheld). For development a bounded deterministic sample (prepare --max-rows N --sample-seed S); time-based holdout (most recent months).
restrictions: SYNTHETIC: never report results as real-world accuracy, real-world validation or BMC performance; keep it on the synthetic/descriptive-of-synthetic tracks, separate from real Indian datasets and from this project's own synthetic data.
Licence is CC BY 4.0 per the Rules; this repository still never commits or redistributes raw or prepared rows.
Complainant-profile columns are sensitive attributes: never features or targets for any task (system design §13). The adapter never stores them.
Contractor/officer/address/contact columns are never read (PII roles).
Post-resolution fields (status, closing time, resolution remarks, reassignment, escalation, satisfaction/rating) must never be inputs for intake or triage — see the per-task column policy.
The source agency/department is a target-side value: it is never converted into an input for department prediction.
Do not commit raw or prepared rows.

supports.how: Stress-test recurrence/hotspot/baseline analytics logic and seed demos on a large Mumbai ward-level synthetic spatio-temporal complaint set.
caveats: Synthetic: demonstrates the pipeline, says nothing about real BMC data.

supports.how: Exercise routing/department-mapping and priority/resolution-time pipelines against our taxonomy (pipeline testing + leakage testing).
caveats: Severity/priority/department may be generated deterministically from category: the determinism audit decides whether a target is usable.
Resolution times are right-censored for unresolved complaints.
Numbers describe the generator, not real municipal behaviour.

supports.how: Realistically-shaped rows to seed a copilot demo database (labelled synthetic).
caveats: Demo realism only; not a model evaluation.

does_not_support.capability: Real-world validation of any CivicConnect capability
does_not_support.why: The data is synthetically generated: agreement with it is agreement with a generator.
Any free text is synthetic, so it cannot be confirmed as citizen-written (and would risk echoing the label); the adapter refuses --confirm-citizen-text for this source.

does_not_support.capability: AI-1 image intake / AI-4 resolution evidence
does_not_support.why: Tabular data: no images, no before/after evidence. 'Resolution process' fields are workflow metadata, not evidence.
None: the data is synthetic and not verified to contain such text at all.
Severity is a generated field, not an independently validated label.
Post-resolution outcome; not part of CivicConnect V1; its test labels are withheld.

known_limitations: Synthetic generation may encode simplistic category→severity/department/SLA rules (determinism audit).
Timestamp semantics (filing vs registration vs closure) must be read from the data dictionary.
privacy_notes: Complainant profile, contractor and any address/contact/officer columns are excluded by policy (never stored), even though the data is synthetic: the exclusion rules stay identical so the same code is safe on any future real municipal data.
expected_schema_notes: User-reported complaint categories (not verified against the file): Pothole/Road Damage; Water Supply Disruption; Solid Waste/Garbage; Drainage Overflow/Flooding; Street Light Failure; Illegal Construction; Encroachment; Tree Fallen/Dangerous Tree; Public Toilet Condition; Water Leakage/Pipe Burst; Noise/Air Pollution; Stray Animal Menace; Health/Epidemic.
Exact column names unknown. The adapter resolves roles by alias and by an explicit operator-supplied --role-map; every other column is 'unclassified' and default-denied.
